title: Does Shallow Alignment Extend to Multimodal Models? Probing Vision-Language Safety Depth

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed

Existing work covers VLM safety alignment broadly and identifies the modality gap as a vulnerability, but does not systematically measure alignment depth (token-level) in VLMs the way Qi et al. did for text-only models. However, the general finding that VLM safety is fragile is well-established.

title: Layer-Wise Localization of Safety: Where in the Network Is Alignment Stored?

novelty_assessment.label: already_solved
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This idea is directly addressed by 'Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models: The Key to LLM Security' published at ICLR 2025. That paper identifies safety layers as a small set of contiguous layers in the middle portion of aligned LLMs, uses cosine similarity analysis and parameter scaling to localize them, and validates across Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-2-7b-chat, gemma-2b-it, and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct. The proposed probe-accuracy-vs-layer plot and activation patching are subsumed by this published work. SafeMERGE (2025) and layer-wise alignment studies further extend these findings.

title: Backdoor Trigger Detectability via Standard Alignment Methods: An Empirical Study

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Anthropic's 'Sleeper Agents' (arXiv:2401.05566, 2024) directly tested whether standard safety training (SFT, RL, adversarial training) removes backdoors and found they persist. DPO has been shown to sometimes remove backdoors (Stanford CS224N study). Mechanistic exploration of backdoor attention patterns (2025) adds depth. However, the specific combination of implanting backdoors, applying alignment, then probing with linear probes is partially novel — existing work focuses on behavioral persistence rather than activation-level detectability post-alignment. The overall finding that alignment does not reliably remove backdoors is well-established.
